name: Tyson Foods

logo.source: en.wikipedia.org infobox logo (Tyson Foods corporate logo (2024).svg)

description: Tyson buys animals and turns them into food. It buys live cattle on the open market, buys hogs mostly from independent producers, and raises chickens through contract farmers on its own feed, then processes the meat and sells it to grocers (Walmart alone is 18.7 percent of sales), restaurants and export markets. Beef, Pork and Chicken are 78 percent of segment sales (computed), so profit is largely the spread between meat prices and animal or feed cost rather than a brand premium: in FY2025 chicken earned $1.43B and prepared foods (Jimmy Dean, Hillshire Farm, Ball Park) $0.90B, while beef lost $1.14B and pork $0.20B as cattle supply tightened. Antitrust accruals ($698M in FY2025) and plant closures also cut results.

businessLines.name: Beef (reportable segment)
businessLines.how: Buys live fed cattle on the open market (no own feedlots), processes them into cuts and case-ready beef and sells to grocers, foodservice and export markets, plus hides and variety meats; it earns the spread between beef prices and cattle cost, which was compressed in FY2025 (average price +9.0%, volume -1.9%) so the segment lost money.

businessLines.name: Pork (reportable segment)
businessLines.how: Buys hogs (mostly from independent producers under procurement agreements), processes them into cuts and sells them; earns the spread between pork and hog prices; FY2025 included $380M of legal accruals.

businessLines.name: Chicken (reportable segment)
businessLines.how: Fully integrated: breeds birds (Cobb-Vantress), independent contract farmers grow them on Tyson feed, Tyson processes and sells fresh, frozen and breaded chicken; profit is the spread between chicken price and mainly feed cost (corn, soybean meal and other feed about 53% of domestic live-chicken cost), and FY2025 gained $340M from lower feed costs.

businessLines.name: Prepared Foods (reportable segment)
businessLines.how: Makes branded frozen and refrigerated foods (Jimmy Dean, Hillshire Farm, Ball Park, Wright, State Fair, Aidells, Gallo Salame) from beef, pork, chicken and other ingredients (some supplied by Tyson's other segments) and sells to grocers, foodservice and convenience stores; average price +3.3% in FY2025 mainly passing through raw-material costs.

businessLines.name: International/Other (segment; International separately reportable from Q1 FY2026)
businessLines.group: segment; International separately reportable from Q1 FY2026
businessLines.how: Foreign operations (China, Malaysia, Mexico, South Korea, Thailand, Saudi Arabia) plus merger and integration costs and Tyson New Ventures overhead; International became its own reportable segment in Q1 FY2026.

brands.name: Jimmy Dean, Hillshire Farm, Ball Park, Wright, State Fair, Aidells, Gallo Salame
brands.note: Prepared Foods brands; segment FY2025 sales $9,930M (17.6% of pre-elimination segment sales, computed)

brands.name: Cobb-Vantress
brands.note: Wholly owned; one of the leading poultry breeding-stock suppliers in the world (10-K); revenue not separately disclosed

brands.name: Tyson New Ventures, LLC
brands.note: Investment arm in new protein and food-technology companies

brands.name: Capacity
brands.note: Beef 11 plants, 155,000 head; Pork 6 plants, 451,000 head; Chicken 167 facilities, 42 million head; Prepared Foods 35 facilities, 72 million pounds (10-K Item 2; the time unit of capacity was not extracted)
